title: Deep Search in Real-World Web Environments
excerpt: Despite substantial progress in Deep Search agents, their ability to conduct end-to-end research in real-world open Web environments remains insufficiently evaluated. Unlike static retrieval settings, information on the real-world Web is distributed across diverse sources, modalities, and heterogeneous formats, often involving complex interaction mechanisms that require agents to autonomously search for, access, and integrate relevant evidence during execution. To address this gap, we introduce the OpenDS task, designed to evaluate agents' ability to perform multi-step deep search in the live, open Web. This task requires agents to autonomously explore the real Web, discover and connect…

ai.summary: The paper introduces a new evaluation framework and methodology for Deep Search agents that operate in real‑world open web environments, addressing challenges of heterogeneous sources and autonomous evidence gathering.
ai.why: Provides developers with benchmarks to assess and improve agents that need to browse and synthesize web information beyond static retrieval.

title: Deep Fusion Memory: A Chunk-Level Parametric Memory for Large Language Models
excerpt: Large language models need effective ways to acquire and use external knowledge beyond what they retain from pretraining. Continued pretraining risks catastrophic forgetting, while retrieval at inference time can add substantial overhead. External parametric memory avoids online retrieval, but constructing its training data requires extensive offline search, and output-level interpolation provides only shallow fusion. We introduce Deep Fusion Memory (DFM), a parametric memory architecture that reduces this construction workload and incorporates learned memory into intermediate hidden states. A causal memory predictor learns to generate memory from the preceding context, using retrieved…

ai.summary: The authors present Deep Fusion Memory, a parametric memory architecture that integrates external knowledge into LLMs without runtime retrieval, mitigating forgetting and overhead.
ai.why: Developers can adopt this approach to extend LLM capabilities with updatable knowledge bases while keeping inference fast.

title: Self-Distilling Future Video Representations for World Action Models
excerpt: World Action Models (WAMs) have emerged as a promising approach to learning generalist robot policies using rich spatiotemporal priors from pre-trained video diffusion models. A recent line of WAMs improves inference efficiency by conditioning a separate action decoder on intermediate future video representations extracted from a single denoising step, avoiding costly iterative denoising required for video generation. This design makes action prediction depend directly on the quality of these future representations. In this paper, we introduce Future REpresentation learning via self-Distillation with temporal context (FRED), a framework that trains WAMs to improve the quality of future…

ai.summary: The paper proposes using a single denoising step from video diffusion models to extract future video representations, which a separate action decoder then conditions on for efficient World Action Model inference.
ai.why: Enables faster robot policy inference by avoiding costly iterative video generation, useful for real‑time control systems.

title: FilmFlow: Agentic System for 3D Virtual Film Cinematography
excerpt: Complex camera motion is central to visual storytelling, yet translating cinematographic intent into controllable, executable camera trajectories remains challenging. We introduce FilmFlow, an agentic framework that converts natural-language instructions or reference videos into explicit camera trajectories for dynamic 3D environments. To generate these trajectories, a Director agent constructs executable camera plans by composing high-level motions from concurrent atomic operations that jointly control translation, rotation, and framing. ai.summary: FilmFlow is an agentic framework that converts natural‑language instructions or reference videos into explicit, executable camera trajectories for dynamic 3D environments by using a Director agent that composes high‑level motions from concurrent atomic operations.
ai.why: It lets developers automate cinematographic camera moves in virtual worlds, reducing manual keyframing effort.

title: What Generation Knows: Unlocking Fine-Grained Understanding in Unified Multimodal Models
excerpt: Fine-grained visual understanding requires distinguishing subtle differences in local attributes and spatial relations, yet remains challenging for existing vision-language models. Unified multimodal models (UMMs) offer a new opportunity through generation pathways that preserve rich visual information complementary to understanding. However, existing generation-assisted understanding methods mainly rely on generative supervision or explicit generation and have not systematically explored direct use of native generation-side representations. ai.summary: The paper proposes a generation‑assisted approach for unified multimodal models that improves fine‑grained visual understanding by preserving rich visual information during generation.

title: RouteWeaver: Weaving Mode Selection and Execution into Unified LLM Routing
excerpt: LLM routing dynamically selects and coordinates heterogeneous language models across diverse tasks. However, existing approaches are largely built around a predefined execution paradigm, such as single-round, multi-round, or agentic routing, which fixes how model calls are organized and limits adaptation to different query needs. We propose RouteWeaver, a unified routing framework that integrates these routing modes within a single LLM policy, jointly learning which mode to use and how to select models within that mode. title: Toward Recursive Self-Improvement in Physical AI
excerpt: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) describes a system that improves not only its behavior but also the process by which it improves. Recent digital agents test this idea by rewriting their own code and checking each version with executable tests. Bringing these mechanisms into the physical world requires learning from partial observations through costly trials, while accounting for changing operating conditions and potentially irreversible consequences. We position RSI within robot learning and trace pathways from improving robot capabilities to improving the processes that generate them. We examine how physical experience can strengthen these improvement mechanisms and when the resulting…

ai.summary: The paper outlines a roadmap for recursive self‑improvement in physical AI systems, discussing challenges of learning from costly trials and adapting to changing conditions in robotics.
ai.why: Highlights research directions that could lead to autonomous robots that iteratively enhance their own capabilities, informing long‑term development strategies.

title: Making MLLM Latents Matter: Factor-Aware Predictive Learning for Cinematic Video Generation
excerpt: Cinematic video generation requires both temporal inference from limited inputs (i.e., sparse rather than frame-by-frame guidance) and factor-aware control of character, scene, action, and camera. Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) offer useful priors for both capabilities, but their representations are not automatically actionable for video generation: a Video Diffusion Transformer (DiT) may bypass them through native conditioning pathways, and using them does not ensure either factor-aware control or generation-compatible temporal prediction. We propose Factor-Aware Predictive Learning (FAPL), which establishes effective MLLM latent use as a shared prerequisite and then targets the…

ai.summary: Researchers propose a factor‑aware predictive learning approach that leverages multimodal large language model latents to guide cinematic video generation via a Video Diffusion Transformer.
ai.why: Offers a way to generate high‑quality video content from sparse inputs, useful for developers building AI‑driven media tools.

title: LaLa-World: Scaling Latent World Models with Natural Language Actions
excerpt: This paper shows that JEPA-style latent world models (LWMs) can learn across diverse domains and data sources by adopting the language-conditioned interface of video generation models. We establish this approach as an effective and efficient basis for planning with imagination and downstream policy fine-tuning. To this end, we introduce LaLa-World, a Language-conditioned Latent World model that learns from simulation and robot trajectories together with broader image and video data. Two designs make this work. First, we describe both numerical actions and visual changes in language, enabling joint training of a single future predictor across heterogeneous datasets. Second, we build the…

ai.summary: LaLa-World introduces a language‑conditioned latent world model that learns from simulations, robot trajectories, and video data, enabling planning via imagination and downstream policy fine‑tuning.
ai.why: Provides a scalable framework for developers building AI agents that need to plan in complex, multimodal environments.

title: Heartbeat Thinking: Speculative Reasoning and Tool Execution While Listening in Realtime Voice Agents
excerpt: Tool-using voice agents often leave users waiting after speech ends, even when actionable information arrives earlier in the request. Speculative approaches begin work during speech, but chunk-bounded or interrupt-on-update generation can truncate a tool call before its arguments are complete. This couples computation time to speech updates, limiting useful work completed in advance. We introduce Heartbeat Thinking, which handles updated input through new Thinker invocations while allowing ongoing invocations and dispatched tools to finish. ai.summary: Heartbeat Thinking introduces a framework that lets voice agents begin tool‑use reasoning while the user is still speaking, updating the reasoning with new input without truncating tool calls.
ai.why: Reduces latency in voice assistants, enabling more responsive and continuous tool execution for developers building real‑time agents.

title: Code2Video-Compass: A Comprehensive Benchmark for General-Purpose Code-Based Video Generation across T2V, I2V, and V2V
excerpt: Code-based video generation offers fine-grained control, targeted editing, and component reuse compared with direct video generation. We introduce Code2Video-Compass, a general-purpose benchmark for code-based video generation across text-to-video (T2V), image-to-video (I2V), and video-to-video (V2V) settings. title: Meta Expert: Cross-Layer Expert Sharing for Storage- and Retrieval-Efficient MoE
excerpt: As model parameters scale up, sparsely activated Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) approaches have become essential for model scaling. However, mainstream models currently adopt hierarchical architectures, where experts in different layers, although topologically independent, exhibit substantial similarity and redundancy in their stored content. Compared to the hierarchically arranged Local Expert in existing mainstream models, we hypothesize that inter-layer shared Meta Expert hold greater potential. ai.summary: Meta Expert proposes cross‑layer expert sharing in Mixture‑of‑Experts models, reducing redundancy and improving storage and retrieval efficiency compared to hierarchical expert designs.

title: RLSplat: Resource-Linear Budget Control for Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting
excerpt: Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting (FF3DGS) reconstructs 3D scenes from images in a single forward pass, making it well-suited to applications that must operate within limited resource budgets. To further improve its practicality, recent budget-controllable FF3DGS methods allow the number of Gaussians to be adjusted at inference, so that the output meets a given storage limit or rendering-latency constraint. However, these methods overlook the cost of inference itself: to produce a representation with the target number of Gaussians, they first predict a dense set of Gaussians and then prune or select from it, requiring nearly constant latency and peak memory regardless of the budget. ai.summary: RLSplat presents a resource‑linear control method for feed‑forward 3D Gaussian splatting that balances inference cost with output quality under strict budget constraints.
ai.why: Enables developers to deploy 3D reconstruction on devices with limited compute or memory while maintaining quality.

title: Policy-Mask: Budget-Aware Adaptation of Diffusion Features to Discriminative Tasks
excerpt: Selecting intermediate features from a frozen diffusion model for discriminative tasks is non-trivial because the useful signal is distributed across the denoising trajectory, network depth, and channels. In practice, this requires choosing a timestep, a block, and a channel subset. Existing methods either fix these choices by hand or optimize only a few extraction hyperparameters, most often the timestep, then reuse the same rule across inputs and budgets. We introduce Policy-Mask, a budget-conditioned policy trained on the downstream objective that jointly selects all three under a prescribed channel budget. ai.summary: Policy‑Mask introduces a budget‑aware method for selecting intermediate diffusion features—timestep, block, and channel subset—to adapt frozen diffusion models for discriminative tasks under compute constraints.
ai.why: Enables efficient reuse of large diffusion models for downstream tasks without full fine‑tuning.

title: WeVisOne-VL: Unified Visual Perception from Objects to Pixels
excerpt: Existing vision-language models (VLMs) remain unreliable for fine-grained visual perception. It supports multiple visual tasks including object detection, referring localization, counting, OCR, segmentation, and matting, enabling localization at any user-specific granularity, from points and boxes to masks and alpha mattes. title: Cola2: Co-Adaptive Hierarchical Language Modeling with Continuous Semantic Compression and Balanced Discrete Generation
excerpt: Hierarchical language generation separates continuous semantic modeling from discrete text realization, but its effectiveness depends on what the latent space compresses and how the discrete generator uses it. We propose Cola2, a framework that jointly studies continuous semantic compression, the balance between reconstruction and generation, and continuous-discrete co-adaptation. Cola2 dynamically segments text into semantic spans, controls the compression rate through auxiliary-loss-free negative feedback, and combines reconstruction and generation supervision to learn compact, predictive latent representations. ai.summary: Cola2 is a hierarchical language modeling framework that jointly optimizes continuous semantic compression and discrete text generation by dynamically segmenting text into semantic spans and using auxiliary-loss-free negative sampling to control compression rates.
ai.why: Offers a technical approach for improving the efficiency and quality of hierarchical text generation models.

title: Beyond Watching and Searching: Benchmarking Agents for Video-centered Deep Research Reports
excerpt: Deep research agents synthesize open-web evidence into long reports, but current benchmarks do not evaluate research centered on a source video. This task has direct practical value because it helps users locate relevant moments, verify claims, reproduce demonstrated procedures, and make informed decisions from video content. excerpt: High-quality image editing requires precise modification of target regions while preserving the content of unrelated regions. ai.why: Developers can create editable image layers programmatically, improving workflows that need repeatable, localized edits.
